evidence_refs.description: The default netrc search now calls os.path.expanduser directly without handling failure.
The base revision caught KeyError from expanduser when HOME was unset and the current UID could not be resolved, returning without netrc authentication.
Normal request preparation invokes get_netrc_auth when trust_env is enabled and no explicit authentication is configured.

findings.technical_rationale: On POSIX, expanduser('~/.netrc') falls back to pwd.getpwuid when HOME is absent, and that lookup can raise KeyError for an unmapped UID, a real configuration in minimal or user-namespaced containers. The removed handler therefore lets ordinary request preparation fail before any network operation. This behavior is unrelated to the URL-parsing vulnerability covered by the newly added test and regresses a deliberately documented supported environment from the base revision.
findings.comment_usefulness_rationale: A comment is actionable because retaining the narrow KeyError guard does not interfere with the security fix, and a regression test can preserve both behaviors.

review_summary: Completed the frozen base-to-head review. Found one supported robustness regression: removal of the expanduser KeyError guard can make normal requests fail in environments with neither HOME nor a passwd entry for the process UID.
